5400.full: epic imperfect ὄλεκον, ionic ὀλέκεσκον, like ὄλλυμι, to ruin, destroy, kill , (Homer) (ML)

5404.full: ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Jer.48:32 40:10, 12 (קַיִץ) * ;] __1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September). __2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Rev.18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).† (AS)

s: to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex
5405.full: ὀχλέω, -ῶ (ὄχλος), [in LXX: Tob.6:7, 3Ma.5:41 * ;] to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex: pass., Act.5:6 (act. absol., = pass., to be in a tumult, 3Mac, l.with; cf. ἐν-, παρ-εν-οχλέω, and see MM, xviii).† (AS)

5406.full: ὄψώνιον, -ου, τό (ὀψον- see: ὀψάριον— and ὠνέομαι), [in LXX: I Est.4:56, 1Ma.3:28 1Mac 14:32 * ;] __1. provisions, provision-money, soldiers' pay: Luk.3:14, 1Co.9:7. __2. Generally, wages, hire: 2Co.11:8; ὄ. τῆς ἁμαρτίας, Rom.6:23 (see Deiss, BS, 148, 266).† (AS)

5407.full: ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.), [in LXX : Wis.13:18 18:3 19:5, 1Ma.6:41 * ;] a journey. Jhn.4:6, 2Co.11:26.† (AS)

5409.full: 1. to make even or level , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to level, equalise , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

5410.full: ὁμολογουμένως adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:31 4Mac 7:16 4Mac 16:1 * ;] __1. as agreed, conformably with. __2. confessedly, by common consent: 1Ti.3:16.† (AS)

5411.full: ionic ὁμουρέω, future -ήσω to border upon, march with , [ οἱ Κελτοὶ, ὁμουρέουσι Κυνησίοισι (Herdotus Historicus) from ὅμορος (ML)

5412.full: ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ (ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; see MM, xviii), [in LXX: Eze.17:18-19 (עָלָה) 1Es 9:93* ;] affirmation on oath, an oath: Heb.7:20-21, 28.† (AS)

5414.full: ὄρθριος, -α, -ον (ὄρθρος), [in LXX: 1Ki.28:14, Job.29:7, 1-25; 3Ma.5:10 3Mac 5:23 * ;] early, in the early morning: Luk.24:22, Rec. (see: ὀρθρινός).† (AS)

s: anything strung like a necklace, a wreath, chaplet
a dance performed in a ring
5416.full: 1. a cord, chain , especially a necklace, collar , (Homer), attic 2. generally, anything strung like a necklace, a wreath, chaplet , (Pindar); στεφάνων ὅρμος a string of crowns, i. e. of praises, (Pindar) 3. a dance performed in a ring , (Lucian) 4. a roadstead, anchorage, moorings , (Iliad by Homer), attic 5. metaphorically a haven, place of shelter or refuge , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 6. = ἕρμα 1, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

5419.full: ὑγρός, -ά, -όν, [in LXX: Jdg.16:7,8 (לַח), Job.8:16 (רָשׂב), Sir.39:13 wet, moist, opposite to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green: Luk.23:31.† (AS)

5420.full: ὑπερ-φρονέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 4Ma.13:1 4Mac 14:11 4Mac 16:2 * ;] __1. to be overproud, high-minded (Æsch.): μὴ ὑ. παρ᾽ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν (on the paranom., see Vau., in l), Rom.12:3. __2. to overlook, think slightly of (Thuc., Plat.).† (AS)

5422.full: 1. the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew , (Thucydides), etc. 2. service , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

s: to cause one to remember, put one in mind or remind one of
5423.full: ὑπο-μιμνήσκω [in LXX: 3Ki.4:3 B ( hi.), Wis.12:1 18:22, 4Ma.18:14 * ;] to cause one to remember, put one in mind or remind one of: with accusative of thing(s), 2Ti.2:14, 3Jn.10; with dupl. accusative (Thus., al.), Jhn.14:26; with accusative of person(s), before περί, 2Pe.1:12; id., before ὅτι, Ju 5; with inf., Tit.3:1; pass., with genitive of thing(s), Luk.22:61.† (AS)

5425.full: ὑπ-έχω [in LXX: Psa.89:50 (נָשָׂא), La 5:7 (סָבַל), Wis.12:21, 2Ma.4:48 * ;] to hold or put under. Metaphorical, to undergo, suffer: δίκην, Ju 7 (Soph., Eur., al.).† (AS)

s: I have laid down the rule
5426.full: 1. to lie under or beneath , (Iliad by Homer); with dative, (Plato Philosophus) 2. in various metaphorically senses, 3. to be put under the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted or proposed to one , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to be laid down or assumed as an hypothesis , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis, (Plato Philosophus); impersonal, ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. to be suggested , (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to be left at bottom, left remaining , (Thucydides) 7. to be subject to, submit to , τινι (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be submissive , (Plato Philosophus) 8. to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged or mortgaged , τινος for a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator) 9. to underlie , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 10. to be subordinate , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to take away underhand, filch away
5428.full: 1. to seize underneath or inwardly , (Homer) 2. to draw or take away from under a thing, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer):—;also τὴν χεῖρα ὑφῄρει tried to draw it away , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to take away underhand, filch away , (Thucydides); ὑφ. τῆς ὑποψίας gradually to take away part of . ., (Thucydides):—;Pass., ὑπαραιρημένος (ionic perfect participle) put secretly away, made away with , (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid. to take away underhand, filch away, purloin , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 4. in Mid. also with accusative pers., ὑφ. τινά τινος to rob him of a thing, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

5429.full: ῥαντίζω [in LXX: Lev.6:27 (20), 4Ki.9:33 (נָזָה), Psa.51:7 (חָטָא pi.) * ;] = cl., ῥαίνω, to sprinkle, besprinkle: with accusative, Heb.9:13, 19; id. and dative, Heb.9:21; pass., Rev.19:13, WH; of cleansing by sprinkling, Heb.10:22 (see M, Gr., ii, 100); mid., Mrk.7:4 (WH, txt., R, mg.).† περι-ραίνω (-ρραίνω, Rec., see WH, App., 139 f.), [in LXX for נָזָה hi. ;] to sprinkle around: Rev.19:13 T (ῤεραντισμένον, WH; ῤε-, R, txt.; βεβαμμένον, Rec., R, mg.).† (AS)

s: In late writers, to strike with the palm of the hand
5430.lxx: in LXX: Jdg.16:25, Heb.11:4, I Est.4:11 *
5430.full: ῥαπίζω (ῥαπίς, a rod), [in LXX: Jdg.16:25, Heb.11:4, I Est.4:11 * ;] __1. prop., to strike with a rod. __2. In late writers, to strike (the face) with the palm of the hand: Mat.26:67; with accusative of person(s), before εἰς τ. σιαγόνα, Mat.5:39 (cf. Field, Notes, 40, 105).† (AS)

5431.full: ῥαφίς, -ίδος, ἡ (ῥάπτω, to sew), a needle: Mat.19:24, Mrk.10:25 (cf. βελόνη).† (AS)

s: a rag, remnant, piece of cloth
5433.full: ῥάκος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Isa.64:6 (5) (בֶּגֶד), Jer.38:11 (סְחָבָה), Est.4:17 * ;] __1. a ragged garment (Hom.). __2. a rag, remnant, piece of cloth: Mat.9:16, Mrk.2:21.† (AS)

s: in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers
In late Greek , a narrow road, lane, street
5434.lxx: in LXX: Isa.15:3 (רְחֹב), Pro.31:23 א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1*
5434.full: ῥύμη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Isa.15:3 (רְחֹב), Pro.31:23 א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1* ;] __1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers. __2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, Mat.6:2, Luk.14:21 Act.9:11 12:10 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).† (AS)

5435.full: ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Isa.4:4 (צוֹאָה), Job.14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;] dirt, filth: 1Pe.3:21.† (AS)

5436.full: a cleft : in (Odyssey by Homer), ῥῶγες μεγάροιο are narrow passages leading to the hall. (ML)

5439.full: Αυσιτιδι Ausis - a name found only in LXX at Job.1.1; 42.17 with no equivalent in the Hebrew text

5441.full: Γαβριήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גַּבְרִיאֵל, hero of God), the archangel Gabriel: Luk.1:19, 26.† (AS)

5445.full: Ζεύς genitive, Διός, dative, Διΐ, accusative, Δία (Δίαν, D, al.), Zeus (Lat. Jupiter): Act.14:12-13.† (AS)

s: Cappadocia, a province of Asia Minor
5447.full: Καππαδοκία, -ας, ἡ Cappadocia, a province of Asia Minor: Act.2:9, 1Pe.1:1.† (AS)

s: Cos, an island in the Ægean Sea
5450.full: Κῶς genitive Κῶ, ἡ, Cos, an island in the Ægean Sea: accusative Κῶ, Act.21:1 (Κῶν, Rec.).† (AS)

5451.full: 1. Linos , a mythical minstrel, son of Apollo and Urania (Calliope), teacher of Orpheus, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), etc. 2. as appellative, the song or lay of Linos , sung by a boy to the cithara while the vintagers are at work, Λίνον ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄειδεν sang the lovely lay of Linos in accompaniment, (Iliad by Homer):—;compare αἴλινος which is a mournful song. (ML)

5453.full: Μωυσῆς (Μωϋσῆς, T; Μωσῆς, Rec.), -έως, dative - (as LXX: Exo.5:20, al.), and -εῖ, accusative -ῆν (ac LXX) and -έα (Luk.16:29 only) (Heb. מֹשֶׁה), Moses: Mat.8:4 17:3-4, al.; νόμος Μωυσέως, Luk.2:22 24:44, Jhn.7:23, Act.13:39 15:5 28:23, 1Co.9:9, Heb.10:28; by meton., of the books of Moses, Luk.16:29 24:27, Act.15:21, 2Co.3:15 (AS)

5457.full: Πέτρος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. a stone, see: πέτρα, Κηφᾶς), Simon Peter, the Apostle: Mat.4:18 10:2, Mrk.3:16, Luk.5:8, Jhn.1:41, 43, al. (AS)

5459.full: Satan , i. e. an adversary, enemy : name for the Devil , (New Testament) Hebr. word. (ML)

5467.full: Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת), Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Luk.4:26.† (AS)

5470.full: Φαρές, ὁ indecl. (Heb. פֶּרֶץ, Gen.38:29), Peres: Mat.1:3, Luk.3:33.† (AS)

5474.full: 1. of persons, regarded with reverence, august, venerable , and of women, deserving respect, tender , (Homer) 2. active shamefaced, reverent , (Odyssey by Homer):—;adverb -ως, reverently , (Odyssey by Homer) 3. comparative αἰδοιότερος, (Odyssey by Homer); Sup. αἰδοιέστατος, (Pindar) (ML)

5475.full: αἰδώς (-όος), -οῦς, ἡ, [in LXX: 3Ma.1:19 4:5 * ;] a sense of shame, modesty: 1Ti.2:9 (for exx., see MM, VGT, see word).† SYN.: αἰσχύνη (see Thayer, 14; Tr., Syn., §xix; Cremer, 611 f.; CGT on I Ti, l.with). (AS)

s: for perception by the senses, perceptive
5478.full: 1. of or for perception by the senses, perceptive , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;adverb αἰσθητικῶς ἔχειν to be quick of perception , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of things, perceptible , (Plutarch) (ML)

5479.full: αἰσθητήριον, -ου, τό (αἰσθάνομαι), [in LXX: Jer.4:19 (קִיר), 4Ma.2:22 * ;] sense, organ of perception: Heb.5:14 (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

s: on the very day, on the same day, immediately
5482.full: 1. made or done on the very day , (Aeschines Orator) 2. adverb αὐθημερόν (oxytone), on the very day, on the same day, immediately , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; ionic αὐτημερόν, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

5484.full: βαθύνω (βαθύς), [in LXX for עמד: Psa.91 (92):5, Jer.29 (49):8 30(49)30 * ;] to deepen: Luk.6:48.† (AS)

5490.full: βασιλίσκος, -ου, ὁ (diminutive of βασιλεύς), [in LXX a basilisk: Ps 90 (91):13 (פֶּתֶן), Isa.59:5 (אֶפְעֶה)* ;] prop., a petty king: Jhn.4:46, 49 WH, mg. (see: βασιλικός).† (AS)

5492.full: βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βεβαιόω, which see), [in LXX: Lev.25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wis.6:19 * ;] confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Php.1:7; εἰς β., Heb.6:16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104ff.; Cremer, 140).† (AS)

5494.full: Causal of βαίνω, to make to mount, to lift up, exalt , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

5499.full: βούλημα, -τος, τό (βούλομαι), [in LXX: Pro.9:10 (דַּעַת), 2Ma.15:5, 4Ma.8:18 * ;] purpose, will: Act.27:43, Rom.9:19, 1Pe.4:3.† SYN.: θέλημα. (AS)
